Add water and a stream network to a MapLibre GL map, styled from the registry

Source: R/gq_mapgl_network.R
gq_mapgl_network.Rd

Lakes and rivers take the registry's lake style, and streams the streams_all style, drawn wider by stream order so a mainstem reads over its headwaters. Water goes on first, so streams draw over it.

Usage

gq_mapgl_network(
  map,
  streams = NULL,
  water = NULL,
  reg = gq_reg_main(),
  ids = c(water = "gq_water", streams = "gq_streams"),
  order_field = "stream_order",
  widths = c(0.6, 3),
  legend = FALSE,
  digits = 5L
)

Arguments

map

A map from gq_mapgl_basemap().

streams

An sf of stream lines, or NULL.

water

An sf of lake and river polygons, or NULL. Keep only the columns you need: every one is written into the page.

reg

A registry, as from gq_reg_main().

ids

Source and layer ids, c(water = , streams = ). Name them to switch them in gq_mapgl_controls().

order_field

The stream order column of streams.

widths

Line width in pixels at order 1 and at order 6 and above.

legend

Add a legend for each layer drawn: Lake, and the stream classes the network holds, or one row named by the registry's first class (Stream) when it carries no feature_code.

digits

Decimal places kept in the coordinates; 5 is about 1 m.

Value

map, with the layers added.

Details

streams_all is classified by FWA feature_code. A network carrying that column is coloured class by class; one without it, as from a fwa_stream_networks_sp query that leaves the code out, is drawn as the registry's first class, Stream, at its opacity.

See also

gq_mapgl_basemap(), gq_mapgl_layer()

Examples

reg <- gq_reg_main()
m <- gq_mapgl_basemap(neexdzii_wsd, "positron") |>
  gq_mapgl_network(streams = neexdzii_streams[c("gnis_name", "stream_order")],
                   water = neexdzii_lakes["gnis_name_1"], reg = reg)
vapply(m$x$layers, `[[`, "", "id")
#> [1] "gq_water"   "gq_streams"
